summary.text: A 69-year-old man, a former smoker of three packs per day with no comorbidities, presented in June 2017 with persistent morning stiffness and symmetric polyarthritis of the hand joints for over 6 weeks. He had no respiratory symptoms. Admission vital signs were recorded and fine crackles were heard over both lungs.

Serology was negative for rheumatoid factor and ACPA, with raised CRP, ESR and KL-6. Joint X-ray showed erosions and ultrasound showed synovial thickening with increased blood flow. Chest radiograph and HRCT showed ground-glass attenuation with traction bronchiectasis in the lower lungs, and he was diagnosed with seronegative RA and RA-ILD.

He started prednisolone, methotrexate and an NSAID. Arthritis activity reached remission about 1.5 years after RA diagnosis, but ILD worsened; prednisolone was raised and methotrexate was replaced by tacrolimus, later stopped for renal dysfunction. Abatacept and then intravenous cyclophosphamide failed to stop progression, and he met criteria for progressive pulmonary fibrosis. Upadacitinib 15 mg daily was then started.

At 29 weeks of upadacitinib, dyspnea grade, GGA on HRCT, pulmonary function and DAS28-CRP improved, although traction bronchiectasis remained. Upadacitinib and prednisolone were tapered, and at the time of publication there were no signs of worsening ILD.
